subject.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers

question: Should OpenClaw core accept this `gateway.peers` session-routing shape now, or hold cross-gateway sessions behind the broader federation/security contract?
rationale: The branch changes gateway trust, message delivery, and session-state ownership; choosing the permanent core API and security model is a maintainer product/security decision, not a mechanical code repair.

options.title: Design the core contract first
options.body: Hold this PR until maintainers define peer identity, URL policy, scopes, replay/idempotency, and session-visibility semantics, likely through the open federation tracker.

options.title: Narrow this PR to configured peers
options.body: Allow a revised PR only if it removes raw URL routing, uses an approved peer config/auth contract, fixes runtime blockers, and supplies real multi-gateway proof.

options.title: Move bridge work outside core
options.body: Keep core gateway-local and expose only missing plugin/API seams for an external bridge or ClawHub package to own cross-gateway routing.

recommendation.title: Design the core contract first
recommendation.body: Hold this PR until maintainers define peer identity, URL policy, scopes, replay/idempotency, and session-visibility semantics, likely through the open federation tracker.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail for sessions_spawn, session helpers, and gatewayUrl SSRF hardening points to this owner candidate for the security-boundary decision.
